title: How this guide fits together
one_liner: Nine lifecycle stages, eight observed failure patterns, and six kinds of record joined by a graph drawn only from cited edges, with a pathfinder that ranks and never recommends.

title: Reading a gate, with its state overlay and its pending changes
one_liner: A gate record is a rule the firm did not write, carried with its governing text, the openings it applies to, the stages it binds, the state law laid over it, and the changes already dated but not yet in force.

title: Reading an effect size
one_liner: What the coefficients on the guide's record cards mean, how to read a correlation, a d and an odds ratio, and how far a number from one firm travels.

title: The clearance process, from sponsorship to access
one_liner: A contractor cannot start a clearance on its own schedule, cannot keep a bench of cleared people, and does not run the clock between an accepted offer and a badge.

title: The cost of a vacancy, in three parts
one_liner: An open requisition costs the firm what it spends to fill it, what the empty seat does to delivery and to the people covering it, and the cash it fronts between payroll and payment; only the first shows on an invoice.

title: The labor category and the wrap rate
one_liner: On a time-and-materials contract each labor category has a fixed hourly rate that already contains the wage, the indirect costs and the profit, and it pays only for people who meet the category's qualifications.

title: What predicts a good hire
one_liner: Scored evidence of the work itself, a structured interview, a knowledge test or a work sample, predicts job performance; an unscored conversation and a count of years on a résumé barely do.

title: Who pays for training
one_liner: Theory says the worker pays for skills any employer can use; in practice the firm pays, keeps part of the return while the person stays, and finds the law narrowing the ways it can hold the investment.

title: Why people leave
one_liner: Wanting to leave and looking are the strongest signals, then commitment, fit, satisfaction, embeddedness and the supervisor; pay is modest and works through comparison; hours as such barely register, strain does.
